body.heading: Sleep likes a runway
paragraphs: You would not expect a plane to land without descending first, yet many of us try to go from bright screens and busy thoughts straight into sleep. Sleep hygiene — the habits and environment around sleep — is a well-established part of healthy sleep advice.
A wind-down routine is simply a descent path: thirty to sixty minutes of gradually dimmer, slower, quieter activity that your body learns to associate with sleep.

body.heading: Build your descent
paragraphs: Pick three or four steps you can repeat most nights: dim the lights, change into night clothes, wash up, read a few pages, set out tomorrow's things. The order matters less than the repetition — routine is the signal.
Keep screens out of the last stretch if you can, or at least switch them to something calm and finite. A chapter ends; a feed never does.

takeaway: Give sleep a runway: the same few calm steps, in the same order, most nights.
